scope: Darwin ARM64, single-threaded precise non-moving generational STW GC; no M19c-f features

object_header.young: old bit clear; new dynamic allocations age=0
object_header.allocation_state: Go free blocks: typeID=0, free bit2 and relative bin link; Mio free blocks: zero header, payload link. Unchanged payload layouts.

metadata.go: 64-byte Heap header, unchanged object origin. 3072-byte metadata after logical object capacity, followed by side entries. side(header)=end+3072+header-origin.
metadata.mio: 3072-byte metadata before logical object capacity, then side entries after end. side(header)=end+header-origin.
metadata.side_entry: two 64-bit native header links: youngNext, rememberedNext. One potential entry per 16-byte object boundary.
metadata.virtual_overhead: one extra capacity-sized side mapping region in the existing mmap; total mapping Go=2*capacity+64+3072, Mio=2*capacity+3072. Sparse pages are touched only by object-start entries. Extra virtual and resident metadata is outside logical object capacity, and must be included in future M19c budgeting.

architecture.minor: Trace exact Shadow Frame roots into Young; skip Old targets. Drain remembered owners using their exact layouts and rebuild only owners that still reach Young. Go uses a fixed-point young-list scan, Mio reuses recursive precise marking. Sweep only Young list; free dead young into existing bins; advance age and promote in place. No physical Old header walk or generic Old payload walk in independent Minor.
architecture.major: Original full precise mark/sweep retained, with flags preserved. Full physical validation/coalescing/bin rebuild remain; Mio suffix trimming remains. Rebuild young and remembered lists after successful collection. Major does not advance minor-survival age.
architecture.remembered_set: Intrusive links in side metadata plus header membership bit ensure idempotent insertion, no fixed-size overflow. Owner-dirty barrier intentionally admits a superset of old owners; actual references are classified ONLY by precise layouts during scan. Scalar int64/address-shaped values never become edges. Deletion is pruned at next Minor. Promotion and Major rebuilding queue old owners, so first subsequent Minor can scan all promoted/rebuilt Old owners once; later minors only scan retained/dirtied owners.
architecture.promotion: Age increment once per surviving independent Minor. At age>=current T set old bit, preserve address/payload/aliases, update counters, queue owner for exact young-edge scan.

adaptation.policy: Three consecutive identical votes before a one-step change. Old occupied bytes >= half capacity or <25% young survival votes up; >50% survival and >=25% of pre-GC Young bytes in age>=2 remaining cohorts votes down. Other evidence resets streak. Age histograms and mature cohort bytes are updated during sweep. Purely deterministic integer arithmetic.

architecture.collection_policy: Allocation normally tries existing bins/bump. On failure runs Minor and retries, then Major and retries once before OOM. Stress runs collection before initial allocation. Both supplement every eighth Minor with Major if any Old exists, bounding dead-old retention; independent Minor remains callable without Major. Back-to-back collection body timings are separate, not a combined safepoint pause SLA.
architecture.allocator: Existing mmap arena, physical spans, cross-page and large buffers, free splitting/coalescing and stable addresses retained. Minor adds dead blocks without an Old walk/coalescing pass; full consolidation remains Major work. All object sizes still use this allocator: no LOS.
architecture.unsupported_native_features: Map opcodes still rejected by both Native AOT paths; immutable struct/enum initialization has no intervening safepoint. No invented native Map/field-mutation syntax is tested.

barrier_audit.owner: backing Storage; exact reference flag controls tracing

barrier_audit.path: push / append_all including aliases and existing capacity

barrier_audit.owner: all newly promoted/rebuilt Old owners, precise pruning on next Minor

barrier_audit.coverage: No collection safepoint between allocation and completion; Storage temporarily protected across descriptor allocation survives at most one Minor, below minimum T=2. No insertion barrier needed while Young. Truncate only removes references and is pruned at next Minor.
Byte Storage data and fresh object construction only; no mutable old managed reference store bypasses the audited paths.

benchmark.baseline: Retained signed M19a current-images verified against historical report hashes and codesign, copied into new evidence. Same Mochi bytes, alternating fixed-seed order, all slow samples retained.
benchmark.environment: Heavy unrelated long-running esbuild processes and repository checks overlapped measurement. Host process snapshot preserved. Identical no-GC control images show substantial latency noise. Interleaved same-session comparisons are recorded; historical M19a absolute tails are not treated as equivalent load conditions.

known_limits: Side metadata reserves an extra capacity of virtual address space and increases RSS for dense small objects; no automatic process/container memory budget exists yet.
Minor does not coalesce the full heap; Major handles consolidation. Same logical capacity need not imply identical fragmentation under all schedules.
Remembered set is an owner superset; first Minor following promotion/Major may scan newly queued Old owners before pruning.
STW, single-threaded; no concurrent Old collection, LOS, admission controller or heap-budget implementation.
Tail measurements are noisy under recorded host contention; no production pause SLA.
m19c_integration_requirements: Account for both side metadata and arena commitment in future budgeting; current capacity is still logical object-region capacity.
LOS/Young LOS would need the same precise root, barrier and side-link ownership contract.
